chunks: Abd al-Wahid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdus al-Naysaburi al-Attar told us, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaybah told us, saying: Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi narrated from Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-Harawi, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them), saying:
The actions of the servants are created. I said to him: O son of the Messenger of God, what is the meaning of 'created'? He said: Predestined.
ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Rida mean when he says human actions are 'created'?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the theological nuance of 'created actions' by equating 'mukhalaqa' with 'mugaddara' (predestined/determined), thereby affirming the Shia doctrine of *al-Amr bayn al-Amrayn* (the matter between the two matters). This explanation reconciles divine omnipotence with human agency, asserting that while God creates the power and capacity for action, humans acquire (*kasb*) the specific deeds through their free will, avoiding the extremes of absolute determinism (*jabr*) and total independence (*tafrid*).

en.basel-kadem: 51.	We were told by Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Yahya al-‘Attar, that he said: We were told by my father, from Hussain bin Hasan bin Aban, from Muhammed bin Ourma, from Muhammed bin Khalid, from Harun, from Mufaddal, from Sa’d al-Khaffaf, from Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him, that he said: Hearts are (of) four (types): a heart in which there is hypocrisy and faith; an overturned heart; a heart that is dispositioned; and a heart that is radiant and lightening. I said: What is the radiant? He said: Within it is like the shape of a lamp. As for the dispositioned, it is the heart of a hypocrite.

As for the radiant, it is the heart of a believer; if Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, gives him, he tanks, and if He tests him, he is patient. As for the overturned, it is the heart of a polytheist. He then recited this verse: «Is the one who walks while overturned on his face, more guided, or the one who walks uprightly on a straight path?» [67:22] As for the heart in which there is faith and hypocrisy, they are a people who were in Ta’if; if the time of one of them approaches firstly to his hypocrisy, he is to perish, and if it approaches firstly to his faith, he is to be saved.
